privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy-policy.body:
Last updated: July 15, 2026

This Privacy Policy describes how TENNIS CLUB (the "Site", "we", "us", or "our") collects, uses, and discloses your personal information when you visit, use our services, or make a purchase from tennisclubfinejewelry.com (the "Site") or otherwise communicate with us regarding the Site (collectively, the "Services"). For purposes of this Privacy Policy, "you" and "your" means you as the user of the Services, whether you are a customer, website visitor, or another individual whose information we have collected pursuant to this Privacy Policy.

Please read this Privacy Policy carefully.

## Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time, including to reflect changes to our practices or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. We will post the revised Privacy Policy on the Site, update the "Last updated" date and take any other steps required by applicable law.

## How We Collect and Use Your Personal Information

To provide the Services, we collect and have collected over the past 12 months personal information about you from a variety of sources, as set out below. The information that we collect and use varies depending on how you interact with us.

In addition to the specific uses set out below, we may use information we collect about you to communicate with you, provide or improve or improve the Services, comply with any applicable legal obligations, enforce any applicable terms of service, and to protect or defend the Services, our rights, and the rights of our users or others.

### What Personal Information We Collect

The types of personal information we obtain about you depends on how you interact with our Site and use our Services. When we use the term "personal information", we are referring to information that identifies, relates to, describes or can be associated with you. The following sections describe the categories and specific types of personal information we collect.

### Information We Collect Directly from You

Information that you directly submit to us through our Services may include:

-
**Contact details** including your name, address, phone number, and email.

-
**Order information** including your name, billing address, shipping address, payment confirmation, email address, and phone number.

-
**Account information** including your username, password, security questions and other information used for account security purposes.

-
**Customer support information** including the information you choose to include in communications with us, for example, when sending a message through the Services.

Some features of the Services may require you to directly provide us with certain information about yourself. You may elect not to provide this information, but doing so may prevent you from using or accessing these features.

### Information We Collect about Your Usage

We may also automatically collect certain information about your interaction with the Services ("**Usage Data**"). To do this, we may use cookies, pixels and similar technologies ("**Cookies**"). Usage Data may include information about how you access and use our Site and your account, including device information, browser information, information about your network connection, your IP address and other information regarding your interaction with the Services.

### Information We Obtain from Third Parties

Finally, we may obtain information about you from third parties, including from vendors and service providers who may collect information on our behalf, such as:

- Companies who support our Site and Services, such as Shopify.

- Our payment processors, who collect payment information (e.g., bank account, credit or debit card information, billing address) to process your payment in order to fulfill your orders and provide you with products or services you have requested, in order to perform our contract with you.

- When you visit our Site, open or click on emails we send you, or interact with our Services or advertisements, we, or third parties we work with, may automatically collect certain information using online tracking technologies such as pixels, web beacons, software developer kits, third-party libraries, and cookies.

Any information we obtain from third parties will be treated in accordance with this Privacy Policy. Also see the section below, _Third Party Websites and Links._

### How We Use Your Personal Information

-
**Providing Products and Services.** We use your personal information to provide you with the Services in order to perform our contract with you, including to process your payments, fulfill your orders, to send notifications to you related to your account, purchases, returns, exchanges or other transactions, to create, maintain and otherwise manage your account, to arrange for shipping, facilitate any returns and exchanges and other features and functionalities related to your account. We may also enhance your shopping experience by enabling Shopify to match your account with other Shopify services that you may choose to use. In this case, Shopify will process your information as set forth in its Privacy Policy and Consumer Privacy Policy.

-
**Marketing and Advertising.** We may use your personal information for marketing and promotional purposes, such as to send marketing, advertising and promotional communications by email, text message or postal mail, and to show you advertisements for products or services. This may include using your personal information to better tailor the Services and advertising on our Site and other websites. If you are an EEA resident, the legal basis for these data processing activities is our legitimate interest in selling our products, according to Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR.

-
**Security and Fraud Prevention.** We use your personal information to detect, investigate or take action regarding possible fraudulent, illegal or malicious activity. If you choose to use the Services and register an account, you are responsible for keeping your account credentials safe. We highly recommend that you do not share your username, password, or other access details with anyone else. If you believe your account has been compromised, please contact us immediately. If you are an EEA resident, the legal basis for these data processing activities is our legitimate interest in keeping our website secure for you and other customers, according to Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR.

-
**Communicating with You and Service Improvement.** We use your personal information to provide you with customer support and improve our Services. This is in our legitimate interests in order to be responsive to you, to provide effective services to you, and to maintain our business relationship with you according to Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR.

## Cookies

Like many websites, we use Cookies on our Site. For specific information about the Cookies that we use related to powering our store with Shopify, see [https://www.shopify.com/legal/cookies](https://www.shopify.com/legal/cookies). We use Cookies to power and improve our Site and our Services (including to remember your actions and preferences), to run analytics and better understand user interaction with the Services (in our legitimate interests to administer, improve and optimize the Services). We may also permit third parties and services providers to use Cookies on our Site to better tailor the services, products and advertising on our Site and other websites.

Most browsers automatically accept Cookies by default, but you can choose to set your browser to remove or reject Cookies through your browser controls. Please keep in mind that removing or blocking Cookies can negatively impact your user experience and may cause some of the Services, including certain features and general functionality, to work incorrectly or no longer be available. Additionally, blocking Cookies may not completely prevent how we share information with third parties such as our advertising partners.

Our website also recognizes the Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal, which enables you to opt-out of certain uses or disclosures of your information. If you notify us of your preference through GPC, we will treat such signal as a valid request to opt out of sharing / targeted advertising for the associated browser or device, and, if we are able to associate the device sending the signal to a Shopify account, we will apply the opt out request to the account as well. To learn more about Global Privacy Control, you can visit [https://globalprivacycontrol.org/](https://globalprivacycontrol.org/). Other than the Global Privacy Control, we do not recognize other “Do Not Track” signals that may be sent from your web browser or device.

## How We Disclose Personal Information

In certain circumstances, we may disclose your personal information to third parties for contract fulfillment purposes, legitimate purposes and other reasons subject to this Privacy Policy. Such circumstances may include:

- With vendors or other third parties who perform services on our behalf (e.g., IT management, payment processing, data analytics, customer support, cloud storage, fulfillment and shipping).

- With business and marketing partners to provide services and advertise to you. Our business and marketing partners will use your information in accordance with their own privacy notices.

- When you direct, request us or otherwise consent to our disclosure of certain information to third parties, such as to ship you products or through your use of social media widgets or login integrations, with your consent.

- With our affiliates or otherwise within our corporate group, in our legitimate interests to run a successful business.

- In connection with a business transaction such as a merger or bankruptcy, to comply with any applicable legal obligations (including to respond to subpoenas, search warrants and similar requests), to enforce any applicable terms of service, and to protect or defend the Services, our rights, and the rights of our users or others.

We have in the past 12 months disclosed the following categories of personal information and sensitive personal information about users for the purposes set out above in _"How we Collect and Use your Personal Information"_ and _"How we Disclose Personal Information"_:

    Category
    Categories of Recipients

- Identifiers such as basic contact details and certain order and account information

- Personal information categories listed in the California Customer Records statute such as basic contact details and certain order and account information

- Commercial information such as order information, shopping information and customer support information

- Internet or other similar network activity, such as Usage Data

- Geolocation data such as locations determined by an IP address or other technical measures

- Vendors and third parties who perform services on our behalf (such as Internet service providers, payment processors, fulfillment partners, customer support partners and data analytics providers)

- Business and marketing partners

- Affiliates

We do not use or disclose sensitive personal information without your consent or for the purposes of inferring characteristics about you.

With your consent we share personal information for the purpose of engaging in advertising and marketing activities, as follows.

We have “sold” and “shared” (as those terms are defined in applicable law) personal information over the preceding 12 months for the purpose of engaging in advertising and marketing activities, as follows.

        Category of Personal Information
        Categories of Recipients

        Identifiers such as name, e-mail address and phone number
        Business and marketing partners

        Commercial information such as records of products or services purchased
        Business and marketing partners

        Usage Data
        Business and marketing partners

## User Generated Content

The Services may enable you to post product reviews and other user-generated content. If you choose to submit user generated content to any public area of the Services, this content will be public and accessible by anyone.

We do not control who will have access to the information that you choose to make available to others, and cannot ensure that parties who have access to such information will respect your privacy or keep it secure. We are not responsible for the privacy or security of any information that you make publicly available, or for the accuracy, use or misuse of any information that you disclose or receive from third parties.

## Third Party Websites and Links

Our Site may provide links to websites or other online platforms operated by third parties. If you follow links to sites not affiliated or controlled by us, you should review their privacy and security policies and other terms and conditions. We do not guarantee and are not responsible for the privacy or security of such sites, including the accuracy, completeness, or reliability of information found on these sites. Information you provide on public or semi-public venues, including information you share on third-party social networking platforms may also be viewable by other users of the Services and/or users of those third-party platforms without limitation as to its use by us or by a third party. Our inclusion of such links does not, by itself, imply any endorsement of the content on such platforms or of their owners or operators, except as disclosed on the Services.

## Children's Data

The Services are not intended to be used by children, and we do not knowingly collect any personal information about children. If you are the parent or guardian of a child who has provided us with their personal information, you may contact us using the contact details set out below to request that it be deleted.

As of the Effective Date of this Privacy Policy, we do not have actual knowledge that we “share” or “sell” (as those terms are defined in applicable law) personal information of individuals under 16 years of age.

## Security and Retention of Your Information

Please be aware that no security measures are perfect or impenetrable, and we cannot guarantee “perfect security.” In addition, any information you send to us may not be secure while in transit. We recommend that you do not use insecure channels to communicate sensitive or confidential information to us.

How long we retain your personal information depends on different factors, such as whether we need the information to maintain your account, to provide the Services, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes or enforce other applicable contracts and policies.

## Your Rights

Depending on where you live, you may have some or all of the rights listed below in relation to your personal information. However, these rights are not absolute, may apply only in certain circumstances and, in certain cases, we may decline your request as permitted by law.

-
**Right to Access / Know**: You may have a right to request access to personal information that we hold about you, including details relating to the ways in which we use and share your information.

-
**Right to Delete**: You may have a right to request that we delete personal information we maintain about you.

-
**Right to Correct**: You may have a right to request that we correct inaccurate personal information we maintain about you.

-
**Right of Portability**: You may have a right to receive a copy of the personal information we hold about you and to request that we transfer it to a third party, in certain circumstances and with certain exceptions.

-
**Right to Opt out of Sale or Sharing or Targeted Advertising**: You may have a right to direct us not to "sell" or "share" your personal information or to opt out of the processing of your personal information for purposes considered to be "targeted advertising", as defined in applicable privacy laws. Please note that if you visit our Site with the Global Privacy Control opt-out preference signal enabled, depending on where you are, we will automatically treat this as a request to opt-out of the "sale" or "sharing" of information for the device and browser that you use to visit the Site.

-
**Restriction of Processing**: You may have the right to ask us to stop or restrict our processing of personal information.

-
**Withdrawal of Consent**: Where we rely on consent to process your personal information, you may have the right to withdraw this consent.

-
**Appeal**: You may have a right to appeal our decision if we decline to process your request. You can do so by replying directly to our denial.

-
**Managing Communication Preferences**: We may send you promotional emails, and you may opt out of receiving these at any time by using the unsubscribe option displayed in our emails to you. If you opt out, we may still send you non-promotional emails, such as those about your account or orders that you have made.

You may exercise any of these rights where indicated on our Site or by contacting us using the contact details provided below.

We will not discriminate against you for exercising any of these rights. We may need to collect information from you to verify your identity, such as your email address or account information, before providing a substantive response to the request. In accordance with applicable laws, you may designate an authorized agent to make requests on your behalf to exercise your rights. Before accepting such a request from an agent, we will require that the agent provide proof you have authorized them to act on your behalf, and we may need you to verify your identity directly with us. We will respond to your request in a timely manner as required under applicable law.

## Complaints

If you have complaints about how we process your personal information, please contact us using the contact details provided below. If you are not satisfied with our response to your complaint, depending on where you live you may have the right to appeal our decision by contacting us using the contact details set out below, or lodge your complaint with your local data protection authority. For the EEA, you can find a list of the responsible data protection supervisory authorities [here](https://edpb.europa.eu/about-edpb/about-edpb/members).

## International Users

Please note that we may transfer, store and process your personal information outside the country you live in. Your personal information is also processed by staff and third party service providers and partners in these countries.

If we transfer your personal information out of Europe, we will rely on recognized transfer mechanisms like the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses, or any equivalent contracts issued by the relevant competent authority of the UK, as relevant, unless the data transfer is to a country that has been determined to provide an adequate level of protection.

## Contact

Should you have any questions about our privacy practices or this Privacy Policy, or if you would like to exercise any of the rights available to you, please call or email us at customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com or contact us at 85 E 10th st, Apt 5J, New york NY 10003-5444, United States.

For the purpose of applicable data protection laws and if not explicitly stated otherwise, we are the data controller of your personal information.

refund-policy.title: Refund policy
refund-policy.body:
Most Tennis Club products are made to order, and cannot be returned for refund. A return for store credit, minus restocking fees, can be requested within 7 business days. All returns are subject to approval.

Please see our [Return Policy](/pages/return-policy) for additional details.

customer-service.title: Customer Service
customer-service.body:
## Availability

### Is the item I am interested in available?
With the exception of some of our basic items, most products from Tennis Club are made to order especially for you! These items are subject to approximately 10-14 business days production time, where they will be hand crafted with love in New York City.

### Is it possible to change or cancel my order after it has been placed?
Yes, you have 48 hours from the time of placing your order to change or cancel. After this period, cancellations will be subject to a 20% restocking fee. Change requests will be reviewed on a case by case basis based on production status of your order.

### Do I need to setup an account to place an order?
You do not need to set up an account to place an order. However creating an account allows you to store your shipping information, see order history, and view your product’s warranty information. Additional features will be added to the account page in the near future.

### When is my credit card charged?
Your credit card will be charged within 24-48 hours from the time you place your order.

### I don't see exactly what I am looking for; can Tennis Club make me a custom order?
Yes, of course! If you do not see the length, stone size, or precious gem that you are most interested in, please let us know at [customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com](mailto:customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com). We can provide you a price estimate for your request as well as production time.
All custom orders will be FINAL SALE.

## Shipping

### What are my options for shipping?
We offer complimentary shipping via FedEx Ground. If you would like to opt into FedEx Priority Shipping for faster delivery, please do so at checkout where an additional fee will be added to your purchase total.

### Where does Tennis Club ship?
We currently ship to the United States, Canada, Mexico, United Kingdom, and Europe. We will continue to launch shipping to other regions — please inquire first if you are interested in placing an order from any other regions.

### When will my order ship?
Most Tennis Club products are made to order, and are subject to approximately 10-14 days production time. You will be notified when your order is ready to ship and provided tracking at that time.

## Returns & Exchanges

### Does Tennis Club accept returns?
Most Tennis Club products are made to order, and cannot be returned for refund. A return for store credit, minus restocking fees, can be requested within 7 business days. All returns are subject to approval.
Please see our [Return Policy](/pages/return-policy) for additional details.

### Contact
Email [customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com](mailto:customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com) with any questions.

return-policy.title: Returns & Exchanges

## Return Policy

Most Tennis Club products are made to order, and cannot be returned for refund. A return for store credit, minus restocking fees, can be requested within **7 business days** of delivery. All returns are subject to approval.

### Eligibility
- Items must be unused, in original condition, and accompanied by original packaging.
- Custom orders are **final sale** and cannot be returned or exchanged.
- Earrings and engraved pieces cannot be returned for hygiene and personalization reasons.

### Restocking
Approved returns for store credit are subject to a restocking fee. Cancellations requested more than 48 hours after purchase may also incur a 20% restocking fee once production has begun.

### How to request a return
Email [customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com](mailto:customerservice@tennisclubfinejewelry.com) within 7 business days of delivery with your order number and reason for return. Our team will review your request and provide next steps if approved.

### Exchanges
Exchanges may be considered on a case-by-case basis depending on production status and stone availability. Please contact customer service to discuss options.

### Refunds
Because most pieces are made to order, Tennis Club does not offer cash refunds on made-to-order jewelry. Where a return is approved, value is issued as store credit.

See also our [Refund Policy](/policies/refund-policy) and [Customer Service](/pages/customer-service) pages.

about-sapphires.title: Sapphire
about-sapphires.body:
_

  _

    **History and Mythology of Sapphire**

Few gemstones carry the weight of history and beauty that sapphire does. For thousands of years, its serene blue has symbolized truth, protection, and divine favor — a link between the heavens and humankind. The word _sapphire_ comes from the Greek _sappheiros_, meaning “blue stone,” though its legend stretches across cultures and centuries.

Ancient Persians believed the sky itself was a reflection of a giant sapphire beneath the Earth; medieval clergy wore it to signify purity and divine truth. Medieval priests wore it to represent purity and insight, while kings believed it protected them from envy and harm. In Asia, sapphires adorned temples and were seen as talismans of spiritual enlightenment. Sapphire has symbolized wisdom, virtue, and celestial power for over 3,000 years. Today, jewelers and collectors continue to celebrate sapphire for its dual nature — timeless yet endlessly variable, a meeting of durability and poetry.

_

  _

    **Sapphire in Art and Jewelry**

Sapphires belong to the _corundum_ family — the same as ruby — and owe their color to trace elements of iron and titanium and chromium that create its dazzling rainbow of shades. Though best known in blue, they appear in every nearly every color of the rainbow (and even color-changing sapphires exist), making sapphire a gemstone of incredible variety. Blue remains the most iconic — with many exceptional blue tones among the most coveted.

Sapphires also played a quiet role in art: during the Renaissance, artists ground the gem into pigment to create ultramarine — the rarest and most precious blue in art. Later, sapphire became a royal favorite, from medieval crown jewels to Princess Diana’s iconic engagement ring.

Today, it’s prized both for its durability and its timeless symbolism of loyalty and clarity. Ranking 9 on the Mohs scale, sapphire is second only to diamond in hardness, a symbol of resilience and integrity. In ancient lore, it guarded against envy and harm; in modern tradition, it embodies loyalty and sincerity — values that make it a favorite of collectors worldwide.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Sapphires

- Ancient Greeks wore sapphires when consulting oracles.

- There are not red sapphires! That’s because red corundum (what Sapphire is made from) is actually called **Ruby**

- The largest known sapphire, the _Star of Adam_, weighs over 1,400 carats.

about-ruby.title: Ruby
about-ruby.body:
_

  _

### **Ruby: The Flame of the Heart**
The ruby has long been called the “king of gemstones.” Its radiant red color has symbolized life, courage, and love since the dawn of civilization. From ancient Burma to the royal courts of Europe, ruby’s fire was believed to hold the very essence of the human heart.

**Mythology and Meaning**In Sanskrit, ruby was _ratnaraj_ — “king of precious stones.” Warriors in ancient India inserted rubies into their flesh to gain invincibility in battle. Burmese folklore told of rubies that could grant safety and success to those who possessed them. In Europe, rubies symbolized passion and protection, and were often exchanged as tokens of love.

_

  _

    **Science and Sources**Ruby is the red variety of _corundum_, colored by chromium. This element also causes ruby’s characteristic fluorescence — a red glow that seems to come from within. The most prized rubies, from Myanmar’s Mogok Valley, are known as “pigeon blood,” valued for their vivid depth and rarity.

**Ruby in Art and Culture**Rubies have graced the crowns of kings and inspired centuries of jewelry artistry — from Mughal treasures to Cartier masterpieces. In modern design, they remain the ultimate expression of emotional fire and timeless devotion.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Rubies

- Ruby’s hardness (9 on the Mohs scale) makes it ideal for heirloom jewelry.

- Rubies were said to boil water when placed in it, symbolizing their heat of passion.

- It’s the birthstone of July and the gem for 40th anniversaries.

about-emerald.title: Emerald
about-emerald.body:
_

  _

    **History and Lore**Emerald has captivated civilizations for over 4,000 years. From Cleopatra’s legendary mines to Mughal emperors and modern haute joaillerie, it remains the symbol of rebirth, love, and divine insight. The name derives from the Greek _smaragdos_, meaning “green gem.”

Revered by ancient Egyptians, Persians, Incas, and Romans, it was said to embody rebirth, insight, and divine favor. Cleopatra’s passion for emerald was legendary — she even gifted visiting dignitaries carved emerald portraits of herself. Ancient Romans associated them with Venus, goddess of love, while medieval mystics used them to predict the future. Their color — soothing and harmonious — was thought to rest the eyes, leading 16th-century gem cutters to gaze into emeralds to relieve strain.

_

  _

This green variety of _beryl_ owes its color to trace chromium and vanadium. Unlike most gemstones, emeralds are known and loved for their inclusions, called _jardin_ (“garden”), which give each gem its own organic landscape. Colombian emeralds from Muzo and Chivor remain the gold standard — deep, vivid, and glowing like captured spring light.

From Mughal engravings and Spanish colonial treasures to Art Deco masterpieces by Cartier, emeralds have left an indelible mark on art and design. Today, they represent growth, peace, and connection — the eternal renewal of life itself.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Emeralds

- Emeralds are always green; lighter or bluish beryls are classed differently (like aquamarine).

- The world’s largest cut emerald weighs over 1.3 kilograms.

- The “Mogul Mughal Emerald” (1695) is inscribed with Islamic prayers and floral motifs.

about-tourmaline.title: Tourmaline
about-tourmaline.body:
_

  _

    **Tourmaline: Nature’s Living Rainbow**

Tourmaline is the gemstone of color itself. Its name comes from the Sinhalese _toramalli_, meaning “mixed gems,” as early traders found crystals of many hues in the same deposits. Tourmaline can appear in every color imaginable — sometimes several in one stone — from pink and green to electric blue, vivid yellow, and black. The famous “watermelon” variety, with a pink core and green rim, is one of nature’s most delightful surprises.

**Scientific and Artistic Wonders**

Ancient legend tells that tourmaline traveled along a rainbow from the earth’s heart, collecting all its colors along the way. This poetic tale suits its scientific reality: tourmaline’s structure allows for remarkable chemical flexibility, making it one of the most diverse minerals on Earth. It’s also pyroelectric and piezoelectric — meaning it can generate an electrical charge when heated or compressed, a property that fascinated Enlightenment scientists.

_

  _

    Symbolism and Modern Appeal
Tourmaline’s symbolism mirrors its diversity. Pink encourages love and compassion, green promotes healing and vitality, black offers protection and grounding, and blue (indicolite) enhances calm and clarity. The neon Paraíba tourmaline, discovered in Brazil in the 1980s, glows with such intensity that it seems lit from within — now among the most valuable gems in the world.

In art and jewelry, tourmaline’s story is one of joyful experimentation. From 18th-century European scientific curiosities to Fabergé’s creations, and now to modern designers exploring ombré gemstone settings, it remains the ultimate expression of color, creativity, and individuality.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Tourmalines

- Paraíba tourmaline from Brazil glows with electric neon hues, among the rarest gems in existence.

- Tourmaline appears in every color — sometimes several in a single crystal.

- Tourmaline is the only gem that’s naturally electrically charged.

- Tourmaline can also appear bi- or tri-colored in a single crystal.

about-tanzanite.title: Tanzanite
about-tanzanite.body:
_

  _

    Tanzanite is a geological miracle — and one of the youngest gemstones known to humankind. Discovered in 1967 and found only in one place on Earth — Tanzania’s Merelani Hills — tanzanite is the gemstone of transformation and rarity. Legend has it that lightning struck the ground, turning brown stones blue, revealing the gem we know today.

According to Maasai legend, lightning struck the slopes of Kilimanjaro, setting the hills ablaze and transforming brown stones into vivid blue crystals — a story that still captures the gem’s almost mystical beauty.

Shortly after its discovery, Tiffany & Co. recognized its potential and introduced it to the world in 1968, naming it “Tanzanite” to honor its singular origin and marketing it as “the most beautiful blue stone discovered in 2,000 years.” It quickly became a favorite among collectors and designers alike.

_

  _

    Tanzanite’s color is famously pleochroic — meaning it displays multiple hues depending on the light and angle. In daylight, it glows sapphire-blue; under warmer lighting, it shimmers violet or burgundy. This optical magic makes every tanzanite unique and dynamic, as though the stone changes with your mood or environment.

Gemologically, tanzanite is softer than sapphire (6–7 on the Mohs scale), requiring careful handling, but its rarity and visual drama have made it a modern icon of fine jewelry. Because its only source is a narrow strip of land just a few kilometers long, geologists estimate the world’s tanzanite reserves could be depleted within a few decades — making every piece a finite piece of Earth’s history.

Symbolically, tanzanite represents transformation, higher consciousness, and new beginnings. It’s often associated with intuition and communication — a bridge between mind and heart. Many believe it helps one articulate truth with grace and calm.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Tourmalines

- Tanzanite is 1,000 times rarer than diamond.

- Only heat can reveal its famous blue color — in nature, the stones are usually brown until gently warmed by volcanic or artificial heat.

- Tanzanite was designated a December birthstone in 2002, alongside blue zircon and turquoise.
- Tiffany’s first marketing slogan for tanzanite was: _“Born of fire, from the heart of the Earth.”_

about-turquoise.title: Turquoise
about-turquoise.body:
_

  _

    **Turquoise: The Sky Stone of Civilizations**Few gemstones hold as deep a cultural legacy as turquoise. With its vivid sky-blue and greenish hues, turquoise bridges earth and heaven, desert and sea, past and present.

**History Across Civilizations**The oldest turquoise artifacts date to 3000 BCE Egypt, adorning the treasures of Queen Zer and Tutankhamun. The word “turquoise” derives from _pierre turquoise_, French for “Turkish stone,” reflecting its trade route origins from Persia to Europe.

 In the Aztec Empire, turquoise mosaics decorated masks and shields of gods. In Native American traditions, it was a sacred stone of protection and spiritual connection.

_

  _

    **Science and Appearance**Turquoise is a hydrated phosphate of copper and aluminum, often veined with matrix patterns from its host rock —yielding shades from soft robin’s egg blue to greenish teal. It’s relatively soft (5–6 on the Mohs scale), making it ideal for intricate carving and inlay. Stabilization techniques today enhance durability while preserving its natural beauty.

**Symbolism and Influence**Turquoise’s symbolism runs deep: it’s a stone of protection, truth, and creative energy. Travelers once wore it as a safeguard against misfortune; artists embraced it as a muse for inspiration.  Its color is psychologically soothing — studies show that turquoise tones promote calm and optimism.

Across cultures, it has always represented vitality and divinity, protection, and communication. Native American tribes — especially the Navajo, Zuni, and Hopi — hold turquoise as sacred, representing the connection between sky and earth, water and life. They used it in jewelry, ceremonial objects, and trade for centuries, believing it brought blessings and balance.  Called _“Ferozah_” by the Persians_,_ it was worn as a talisman of protection and victory, its color symbolizing heaven.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Turquoise

- Turquoise was one of the first gemstones ever mined — over 6,000 years ago.

- Turquoise is one of the only gemstones to have a color named after it!

- Turquoise is one of the official birthstones for December and is associated with the zodiac signs of Sagittarius and Pisces.

- In ancient Persia, people believed turquoise changed color to warn its wearer of danger.

about-diamonds-tennis-club.title: Diamond
about-diamonds-tennis-club.body:
_

  _

### **Origins and History**
Natural diamonds are among the oldest treasures on Earth — some formed over **3 billion years ago**, deep beneath the planet’s crust. Created from pure carbon under immense heat and pressure, each diamond’s journey began long before humanity itself. Ancient Greeks believed they were **“tears of the gods,”** while Sanskrit texts called them _vajra_, the thunderbolt — unbreakable and divine.

Through history, diamonds have adorned royalty, warriors, and artists alike. From the **Koh-i-Noor** to the **Hope Diamond**, they’ve symbolized both celestial purity and earthly power.

_

  _

### **Meaning and Symbolism**
The name “diamond” comes from the Greek _adamas_, meaning **“unconquerable.”** That strength, both literal and symbolic, defines its enduring legacy. Diamonds represent **eternal love, clarity, and truth**, making them the natural choice for engagement rings.

While colorless diamonds remain iconic, nature produces them in every shade — from soft **champagne and yellow** to rare **pink, blue, and green** tones. Each hue reflects unique conditions deep within the Earth, a reminder that beauty often forms under pressure.

### **In Jewelry and Art**
For centuries, diamonds have inspired artisans and designers. During the Art Deco era, they became symbols of modernity and sophistication; today, they remain the cornerstone of fine jewelry design, valued for their unmatched **brilliance and fire**.

Their versatility makes them timeless — whether as center stones or delicate pavé details, diamonds transform light into emotion. Each one is a piece of ancient Earth, cut to capture eternity in a moment of sparkle.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Diamonds

- Diamonds are composed of **pure carbon** — the same element as graphite, arranged in a different crystal form.

- Only about **20%** of mined diamonds are gem-quality.

- They’re the **birthstone of April**, symbolizing strength and endurance.

- Trace elements and atomic shifts create natural colors like pink, blue, or yellow.

about-lab-diamonds.title: Lab Diamonds
about-lab-diamonds.body:
_

  _

    **Lab Diamonds: The Future of Ethical Luxury**Lab-grown diamonds are revolutionizing the jewelry industry, combining scientific innovation with timeless beauty. These diamonds are _real diamonds_ — identical in composition, brilliance, and durability to mined ones — but created in controlled laboratory conditions that replicate the Earth’s natural process.

**Science and Creation**There are two main methods: **HPHT (High Pressure High Temperature)** and **CVD (Chemical Vapor Deposition)**. Both mimic the natural growth of diamond crystals using carbon, heat, and pressure, producing gems that are visually and chemically indistinguishable from mined diamonds.

_

  _

    **Ethics and Sustainability**Lab diamonds offer a transparent, conflict-free origin and significantly lower environmental impact. They require no mining and use fewer resources, aligning with the growing demand for sustainable luxury.

**Modern Symbolism**They symbolize progress, innovation, and conscious choice — beauty without compromise. Modern couples increasingly choose lab diamonds for their ethical story and affordability, allowing for larger carat sizes and bolder design.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Lab Diamonds

- Lab diamonds are 100% carbon, just like mined diamonds.

- NASA uses synthetic diamonds in technology due to their strength.

- The largest lab-grown diamond ever cut weighs over 30 carats.

about-spinel.title: Spinel
about-spinel.body:
_

  _

    **Spinel: The Hidden Royal Treasure**For centuries, spinel lived a life of mistaken fame shining in royal crowns under the wrong name. Many of history’s “rubies” — including the British Crown’s _Black Prince’s Ruby_ — are actually spinel. Its name comes from the Latin _spina_, meaning “thorn,” describing the pointed shape of its crystals.

**History and Rediscovery**Spinel’s vivid reds and pinks once adorned the treasures of Mughal emperors and European monarchs, though it was often confused with ruby. Only in the 18th century did gemologists distinguish the two. Today, spinel’s natural purity and unenhanced color have earned it newfound prestige among collectors.

In ancient Burma, warriors wore red spinel for protection in battle, believing it brought courage and victory. In modern jewelry, its subtle color variations and rare transparency have made it a favorite of connoisseurs who value uniqueness over convention.

_

  _

    **Symbolism and Variety**Spinel occurs in a breathtaking range of colors — from vivid red and pink to lavender, blue, grey, and even black — thanks to trace elements like chromium, cobalt, and iron. With a hardness of 8 and exceptional brilliance, it rivals the finest rubies and sapphires. Yet unlike them, most spinel is never treated — a gem as pure as it is beautiful.

Across cultures, spinel symbolizes renewal, strength, and inner vitality — a fitting reputation for a gemstone that has reclaimed its own identity.

Spinel’s rediscovery has sparked a quiet renaissance. Its pastel purples and greys pair perfectly with contemporary aesthetics, while its vivid reds and pinks recall the regal opulence of Mughal India. Today, spinel stands as the gem lover’s secret — understated, natural, and eternally radiant.

_

##
                Fun Facts about Spinel

- The “Timur Ruby” of the British Crown Jewels is actually a 352-carat red spinel.

- Because of its clarity and rarity, fine spinel was once worth more than ruby.

- Spinel is the birthstone for August, shared with peridot.

- Spinel rates 8 on the Mohs scale, making it ideal for fine jewelry.
